title: Find if Digit Game Can Be Won
statement:
Every value in `nums` is a positive integer with one or two digits. Alice must take either all of the one-digit values or all of the two-digit values, and Bob gets every value she did not take. Alice wins only when her total is strictly larger than Bob's total.

Return `true` when at least one of her two options wins, and `false` when neither does.
notes:
## Intuition

Each value is either one-digit (1 to 9) or two-digit (10 to 99), so `nums` splits into exactly two groups. Whichever group Alice takes, Bob receives the other one, so the game is just "group sum against group sum". Trying both options works, but it simplifies further: Alice takes the group with the larger sum and wins, unless the two sums are equal, in which case either choice is a tie and a tie is a loss.

## Approach

1. Walk through `nums` once.
2. Add each value below 10 to `singleSum` and every other value to `doubleSum`.
3. Return whether the two sums differ.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 10]`: the values 1, 2, 3 and 4 go to `singleSum`, which ends at 10; the value 10 goes to `doubleSum`, which also ends at 10. The sums are equal, so whichever group Alice takes she ties 10 against 10, and the answer is `false`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the values.
- Space: O(1): two running sums.

## Pitfalls

- A tie is not a win: Alice needs a strictly larger total.
- 10 already has two digits: test `num < 10`, not `num <= 10`.
- Compare the two groups with each other. Bob's total is the other group, not the whole array.
- Alice cannot hand-pick values; she must take a whole group.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `singleSum` | total of the one-digit values |
| `doubleSum` | total of the two-digit values |
| `num` | the value being sorted into a group |

narration.2: Running total of the one-digit values.
narration.3: Running total of the two-digit values.
narration.5: Values from 1 to 9 have one digit.
narration.6: Add it to the one-digit group.
narration.8: Anything from 10 to 99 joins the two-digit group.
narration.11: Alice takes the larger group and wins, unless the sums are equal and every choice ties.
